description: Data-analysis task: explain a Q3 churn increase for finance. Two decisions with reasons and rejected options, a number, a command and a line of pandas code to reproduce verbatim, a corrected customer count, a renamed notebook, an abandoned downloads folder and a fake password pasted into the chat.

probes.question: What did we decide about how to define churn, why, and which option did we reject?
probes.answer: Churn means no successful payment for 75 days. A customer is churned on the first day the payment gap exceeds 75 days. We chose this because silent lapses are real churn and the cancel_flag misses many of them. Rejected: using cancel_flag as the churn definition, and treating downgrade to the free plan as churn (kept as a separate outcome instead).

facts.fact: Churn means no successful payment for 75 days
many customers lapse without ever pressing cancel, so the cancel flag misses a large share of real churn

probes.judge_notes: All three key facts are stated, with the rejected option and reason matching the reference.

probes.question: What did we decide about which model to fit, why, and what did we rule out?
probes.answer: We fit a logistic regression with an L2 penalty so finance can read the coefficients and odds ratios. Rejected: gradient-boosted trees, because they cost explainability and the user judged that added complexity would add little.

facts.fact: finance needs coefficients they can read and explain, and a more complex model would add little

probes.judge_notes: Logistic regression, the explainability reason, and the rejected gradient-boosted trees are all stated.

probes.question: Which churn signal did we decide not to use, and what was the reason?
probes.answer: The cancel_flag column was not used as the churn definition. It only captures customers who actively cancelled and misses many silent lapses. Downgrade to the free plan was also not adopted as churn.

facts.fact: many customers lapse without ever pressing cancel, so the cancel flag misses a large share of real churn

probes.judge_notes: The answer correctly says cancel_flag was not used and gives the silent-lapse reason.
